claim.pdf_says:
5)  For each parameter that is passed by value there shall be a corresponding parameter in the invoked method that:

    a)  is specified with the BY VALUE phrase

[page break]

    b)  if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly.

-- two separate lettered list items, a) ending the printed page and b) opening the next.
claim.markdown_says: a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly. (ISO_COBOL.md line 12016; the following line is the anchor, and page 275 begins directly at item 'c)')
claim.why_it_matters: Rule 5)b) has lost its status as an independent lettered rule: its label 'b)' is now mid-sentence inside rule 5)a), so a search for 'b)' under this conformance rule 5 finds nothing and an automated rule extractor sees rule 5) as having items a), c), d) with a) carrying two unrelated requirements. The text itself is intact but the list structure is corrupted at the page seam.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages at 300 dpi. PDF page 274 (printed folio 244) ends its body text with the single line 'a) is specified with the BY VALUE phrase', hanging-indented under '5) For each parameter that is passed by value there shall be a corresponding parameter in the invoked method that:', with nothing after it but the '244 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' footer and the license line. PDF page 275 (printed folio 245) opens with a fresh hanging-indented lettered item 'b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase, shall be specified with the OPTIONAL phrase. No further checking is performed on this parameter and this parameter is considered to match exactly.', followed by c) and d). The two items are unambiguously separate list entries in the source: separate 'b)'/'c)' labels in the label column, separate paragraph blocks, and the b) block starts a page. ISO_COBOL.md line 12016 concatenates them into one line inside the page-274 block -- 'BY VALUE phrase b) if the passed parameter ...' -- and line 12018 is the anchor, with the page-275 body resuming at line 12023 with 'c) if the parameter ...'. So item b) is both (i) stripped of its list-item boundary and (ii) hoisted out of page 275 into the page-274 block. This is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation: the transcription's own convention elsewhere is exactly one lettered item per line -- the structurally identical rule 4) immediately above keeps a), b), c), d) on separate lines 12006/12008/12010/12012, and the b) text there is verbatim identical to the merged text here. Only the item that straddles the page seam was merged, so this is a transcription defect at the seam rather than a stylistic choice. Consequence is real for a spec-citation-driven compiler: rule 5)b) is no longer addressable as a discrete rule, and a line-anchored or list-aware extractor reads rule 5) as a), c), d) with a) carrying two requirements.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed real, with two refinements to the claim's rationale. (1) The claim overstates the search impact: the literal characters 'b)' survive mid-line, so a raw substring search for 'b) if the passed parameter is specified with the OMITTED phrase' does still hit line 12016. What is lost is the structural boundary -- the line/paragraph break and hanging-indent that make it a discrete list item -- so it is line-anchored, list-aware, and rule-extraction tooling that fails, not plain grep. (2) The claim describes only the merge; the defect is also a page-attribution error, since the b) text is printed on PDF page 275 but appears inside the ISO_COBOL.md page-274 block, ahead of the page-275 anchor. Also corroborating, and worth fixing in the same edit: the sibling items on the following markdown page (lines 12023 and 12025, 'c)' and 'd)') sit at zero indent instead of the three-space sub-item indent used for 4)a)-d) and 5)a), so the whole 5)a)-d) sub-list is de-nested from rule 5) across the seam. Correct fix: split line 12016 before 'b)', move the b) item below the anchor to match the printed page, and re-indent 5)b), 5)c), 5)d) to three spaces to match rule 4).
